questions.q: Which type of quant role typically tests C++ fundamentals most heavily, and why?
options: Research-flavored roles, because pandas requires C++ knowledge
Latency-sensitive roles like market making and high-frequency trading, because execution speed in production is the core of the job
All quant roles equally, with no distinction by function
Only roles with no programming component
questions.explain: Latency-sensitive trading and infrastructure roles test C++ because production execution speed is central to the work, while research-flavored roles more often test Python/pandas.

questions.q: In the max-profit coding example, what single-pass pattern solves the problem in O(n) time?
options: Sorting the price array first, then scanning it
Tracking the minimum price seen so far and the best profit seen so far while scanning the array once
Comparing every pair of days with nested loops
Recomputing the full array average on every step
questions.explain: The O(n) solution tracks a running minimum price and a running best profit, updating both in a single pass rather than checking every day-pair combination.

questions.q: What is RAII in C++, and why does it matter for a trading system?
options: A networking protocol used in exchange connectivity
An idiom tying a resource's lifetime to an object's scope, so memory is released automatically rather than depending on a manual free() call that's easy to miss on an exception path
A type of database index used for storing tick data
A rule that forbids the use of pointers entirely
questions.explain: RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) ties resource cleanup to object scope, avoiding manual memory-management bugs, which matters in reliability-critical trading infrastructure.

questions.q: Why is `df["ret"] = df["price"].pct_change()` typically much faster than looping over DataFrame rows in plain Python?
options: Because pandas secretly runs on a different programming language chosen at random
Because the vectorized operation executes in compiled C code and avoids the per-element overhead of the Python interpreter loop
Because looping over rows is actually just as fast in practice
Because pct_change() does not perform any real computation
questions.explain: Vectorized pandas/NumPy operations drop into compiled C code and process the whole array at once, avoiding the repeated interpreter overhead a native Python for-loop pays per element.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a pointer and a reference in C++ relevant to interview questions?
options: There is no meaningful difference between them
A pointer can be null and reassigned to point elsewhere; a reference must bind to a valid object at creation and cannot be rebound
References are always slower than pointers in every case
Pointers can only be used with primitive types, never objects
questions.explain: A pointer can be null and reassigned, while a reference must be bound to a valid object when created and stays bound to that object — a distinction interviewers commonly probe.
